examInfo.format: 12 Single Choice + 4 Multiple Choice (Prüfungsstil, mit Rechenfragen)
examInfo.grading: Übungsset ohne Note — Ziel: ≥ 60 % der Punkte

questions.text:
A retailer has an annual demand of D = 2'400 units, order costs of S = CHF 30 per order and holding costs of H = CHF 4 per unit and year.

What is the economic order quantity (EOQ)?
Same data as before (D = 2'400, S = 30, H = 4). What are the total annual ordering and holding costs at the EOQ (excluding purchase costs)?
questions.explanation: Bestellkosten = D/Q·S = 12.65·30 ≈ 379.5; Lagerkosten = Q/2·H = 94.87·4 ≈ 379.5. Beide sind im Optimum gleich: Total ≈ 759.

questions.text: The holding cost rate H doubles while D and S stay constant. How does the EOQ change?
questions.explanation: Q* ∝ 1/√H. Doppeltes H ⇒ Q* sinkt auf 1/√2 ≈ 0.71 (−29 %). Mehr Bestellungen bei kleineren Losen.

questions.text:
EPQ: D = 3'600 units/year, production rate p = 12'000 units/year, S = CHF 200, H = CHF 6 per unit and year.

What is the average inventory level?

Quantity discount: D = 1'000 units/year, S = CHF 20, holding cost rate 20 % of the price. Price CHF 10.00 for orders of 1–149 units, CHF 9.50 for orders from 150 units.

Which order quantity minimises the total annual costs?
questions.explanation: Stufe 1: H = 2, EOQ = 141 (zulässig) ⇒ TC ≈ 10'283. Stufe 2: H = 1.90, EOQ = 145 < 150 ⇒ Q = 150 (Untergrenze), TC = 133 + 143 + 9'500 ≈ 9'776. Stufe 2 ist günstiger (Einsparung ≈ 507). Einkaufskosten D·p nicht vergessen.

questions.text:
Daily demand has a standard deviation of σ = 15 units, the lead time is L = 9 days, the target service level is 95 % (z = 1.645).

How large is the safety stock?
questions.explanation: SS = z·σ·√L = 1.645·15·3 ≈ 74.0. Wer L statt √L einsetzt, erhält 222 (1.645·15·9).

questions.text:
Average demand is 40 units/day, the lead time is 5 days, the safety stock is 50 units.

At which inventory level (reorder point) should a replenishment order be placed?

Newsvendor: selling price CHF 12, purchase cost CHF 7, salvage value CHF 2, demand ~ N(300, 50²).

What is the optimal order quantity?

Newsvendor: Cu = CHF 30, Co = CHF 10, demand ~ N(200, 40²) (σ = 40, not 40²).

What is the optimal order quantity?
questions.explanation: CR = 30/40 = 0.75 ⇒ z = NORM.S.INV(0.75) = 0.674 ⇒ Q* = 200 + 0.674·40 ≈ 227. Mit σ² = 1'600 anstelle von σ wäre das Ergebnis falsch.

questions.text: The demand during lead time has σ = 25 units. By how many units does the safety stock increase if the service level is raised from 95 % to 99 % (z = 1.645 → 2.326)?
questions.explanation: SS(95 %) = 41.1, SS(99 %) = 58.2 ⇒ +17.0 Einheiten. Die letzten Prozentpunkte Servicegrad sind überproportional teuer.

questions.text:
Periodic review with target inventory: μ = 100 units/week, σ = 20 units/week, lead time L = 2 weeks, z = 1.28. The target inventory is μ·(L+1) + z·σ·√(L+1). Current stock is 150, pipeline 80.

How many units are ordered?
In an ABC analysis of annual expenditure, A-products are those that…

choices.text: are the cheapest items per unit
account for about 80 % of the period costs (with a small share of the items)
account for about 20 % of the period costs

questions.explanation: A = wenige Artikel mit ca. 80 % des Wertanteils; B ca. 15 %, C ca. 5 %. Es zählt der Jahresverbrauchswert (Preis × Menge), nicht der Stückpreis.

sections.title: Part B – Multiple Choice (4 Points)
sections.description: At least two answers are correct. Only the complete correct combination scores (no partial points).

questions.text: Which statements about the EOQ model are correct?

choices.text: The model minimises the sum of order costs and holding costs.
The average inventory is Q*·(1 − D/p)/2.
Replenishment is assumed to happen instantaneously.
Higher order costs lead to a smaller EOQ.
At the optimum the order costs equal the holding costs.

questions.explanation: EOQ: Trade-off Bestell- vs Lagerkosten; sofortige Wiederauffüllung; im Optimum gleich hohe Kostenanteile. Der Ø-Bestand ist Q*/2 (die andere Formel gehört zum EPQ). Höhere Bestellkosten S erhöhen Q*.

questions.text: Which statements about EOQ and EPQ are correct?

choices.text: EPQ and EOQ use the same total cost formula without any change.
The average inventory in the EPQ model is Q*/2.
The EPQ lot size is larger than the EOQ lot size for the same D, S, H.
For p → ∞ the EPQ turns into the EOQ.
EPQ assumes a finite production rate p > d.

questions.explanation: EPQ: Q* = √(2DS/(H(1−d/p))) > EOQ; für p → ∞ ⇒ 1 − d/p → 1. Ø-Bestand EPQ = I_max/2 = Q*(1−d/p)/2, nicht Q*/2.

questions.text: Which statements about quantity discounts (all-units) are correct?

choices.text: The holding cost per unit may differ per price tier if it is a percentage of the price.
If the EOQ of a tier is below its lower bound, the lower bound is the candidate quantity.
The EOQ of the cheapest tier is always optimal.
The total costs must include the purchase costs D·p.
The lower price applies to all units of the order once the threshold is reached.

questions.explanation: All-units: Preis gilt für die ganze Bestellung. H = i·p variiert. TC = Bestell + Lager + Einkauf. EOQ < Untergrenze ⇒ Untergrenze testen. Die billigste Stufe ist nicht automatisch optimal – alle zulässigen Stufen vergleichen.

questions.text: Which statements about the newsvendor model are correct?

choices.text: The critical ratio is Cu/(Cu + Co).
A service level of 100 % is achievable for any demand distribution.
It is best suited for long-living products with stable demand.
It is suited for perishable goods with a short product life and volatile demand.
If the critical ratio CR is below 0.5, the order quantity should be below the mean demand.

questions.explanation: Newsvendor: einperiodig, verderbliche Güter. CR = Cu/(Cu+Co); CR < 0.5 ⇒ Überschuss teurer ⇒ vorsichtig bestellen. 100 % Servicegrad ist bei unsicherer Nachfrage nicht erreichbar; langlebige Güter mit stabiler Nachfrage → EOQ/ROP.
